item.research_question: How can the surface mechanical properties and wear behavior of SS410 steel be enhanced through the reinforcement of gas-atomized AlCrCoFeNi High Entropy Alloy (HEA) particles using Friction Stir Processing (FSP), and what are the optimal process parameters for minimizing wear rate?
item.material_system: AlCrCoFeNi equimolar High Entropy Alloy (HEA) powder reinforced on SS410 stainless steel substrate
item.processing_route: Friction Stir Processing (FSP) using a pinless tool to compact powder in a trapezoidal groove (4 mm depth, 3:1 width ratio) followed by a tungsten carbide tapered pin tool (16 mm shoulder diameter, 4.5 mm length, 4 mm pin diameter); parameters: 900 rpm rotational speed, 20 mm/min traverse speed, 10 kN applied load
item.test_conditions: Microhardness (100 gf load, 15 s dwell); Tensile testing (transverse direction); Wear testing (Pin-on-disc tribometer) with applied load (10–50 N), sliding distance (500–2500 m), and sliding velocity (0.5–2.5 m/s)
key_findings: Microhardness increased by 41.3% to 482 HV at the center of the Stir Zone (SZ).
Ultimate tensile strength increased by 39.1% to 832 MPa compared to the FSP-base metal.
Mean grain size in the SZ was refined to 2.84 μm (range 0.347 μm–8.5 μm).
High Angle Grain Boundaries (HAGB) fraction reached 49.7%.
The regression model for wear rate prediction showed R² = 95.41% and adjusted R² = 94.89%.
Confirmation tests showed an error percentile within ±4% between predicted and experimental wear rates.
Applied load was identified as the most influential factor on wear rate, followed by sliding velocity and sliding distance.
The wear rate decreased with increasing sliding velocity due to protective oxide layer formation.
item.mechanism: Enhancement is attributed to grain refinement via discontinuous Dynamic Recrystallization (DRX) and Severe Plastic Deformation (SPD), the Hall-Petch relationship, Particle Stimulated Nucleation (PSN) mechanism, Zener pinning (barrier effect) hindering grain growth and dislocation movement, and the load-bearing capacity of HEA particles. The formation of an oxide layer at higher sliding velocities also protects the surface against adhesive wear.
item.limitations: Surface modification is limited to a few extensions; the process is ineffective for soft and brittle materials; and the FSP tool design significantly influences grain refinements.
item.future_work: Application of HEA-reinforced FSP samples in the fabrication of surgical equipment, aircraft bearings, and the repair/maintenance of boilers and storage tanks in nuclear and chemical industries.
quotes: The microhardness and ultimate tensile strength of the FSP-HEA sample are increased by 41.3 % and 39.1 % respectively due to the high degree of refined grains with 2.84 μm and evenly distributed HEA particles.
The minimum wear rate is achieved by optimum process parameters along with higher hardness through particle-stimulated nucleation mechanism, Hall-Petch relation, and dynamic recrystallization.
The error percentile of experiments is within ±4 %. Hence, the developed regression model demonstrated a feasible way to predict the wear rate effectively.
